description: Create professionally formatted Excel files with openpyxl, parse complex investment-banking .xlsm models that openpyxl chokes on or silently mangles using stdlib zipfile+XML, and drive the Excel window on macOS via AppleScript without a hung `osascript` call blocking forever. Use whenever the user asks for a polished/professional Excel report (not a bare data dump), mentions borders/number-formats/header-styling in a spreadsheet, references a large or complex .xlsm/.xlsx file (especially from an investment bank, broker, or financial model) that openpyxl fails to open or returns wrong/empty values for, or wants to scroll/zoom/select/activate Excel on their Mac programmatically. Also trigger when openpyxl raises an error, hangs, or silently drops cells on a real-world workbook — that is the signal to switch strategy, not to keep patching openpyxl calls.

results.query: Build me a formatted quarterly sales report as an Excel file, not just a raw data dump.
This .xlsm investment-bank model throws an error in openpyxl — can you parse it anyway and pull out one sheet?
Scroll the currently-open Excel window to cell B12 and zoom to 150%.
I need a professional-looking spreadsheet — borders, header shading, currency formatting on the totals.
Extract just the 'Assumptions' sheet from this big xlsm financial model.
Automate control of the Excel window on my Mac via AppleScript — select a range, then zoom.
The sheet names came out mangled after parsing this xlsm — fix the corrupted names.
Create an .xlsx with a totals row and proper number formatting for these monthly figures.
This xlsm is over a megabyte and openpyxl is choking on it — parse it a different way.
Export this pandas DataFrame to a plain CSV file.
There's a broken formula in this Google Sheet — can you fix it?
Write a VBA macro for this Excel workbook that auto-formats new rows on entry.
Read this 10-row CSV and tell me the column totals.
Convert this Word document into a PDF.
Control the open Numbers spreadsheet window on my Mac via AppleScript — scroll and zoom in.
Based on these numbers I'll type out here, what's driving the increase in Q3 revenue?
Scroll the open PDF viewer to page 12 and zoom in on the chart.
Generate a PowerPoint deck summarizing this quarter's numbers.
